applies_to: All thesis researchers inheriting pumlsc-shared.sty, after central approval
scope: student-facing manuscript prose, captions and abstracts
not_scope: font/layout .sty rules, private evidence IDs, internal JSON/CSV, code identifiers
principles: Researcher-facing prose must reflect the named author's genuine observations, methods and conclusions: no unsupported first-person events or manufactured fieldwork.
Prefer natural scientific prose and, when first-person perspective is appropriate under the university/supervisor guidance, use I/my/we with correct past tense for completed observations and work.
Do not refer to the student author as 'the researcher' or 'the practitioner' merely to make their firsthand observations sound independently collected.

Do not print internal evidence identifiers such as SAFAL-PHOTO-W02B-01, W01/W02/W03, artifact keys, A9, ChatGPT, or control-tower terminology in narrative captions, headings or abstracts. Keep identifiers in private machine-readable evidence registries.
Preserve third-person language when genuinely discussing another researcher, an interview participant, or cited sources; do not mechanically replace all occurrences.
Distinguish witnessed conditions from technically diagnosed causes, actual repaired work from mere defects, and verified incremental costs/delays from respondent estimates.
Do not conceal or falsify the use of writing assistants, research support or generated code; follow institutional disclosure rules.
Version source before compiling outputs: a PDF is derived from a Git source commit and documented private dependencies. Preserve immutable prior version refs, manifests and output hashes.
Project-specific prose and voice policy must live in researcher source and semantic lint guidance, not in the universal typographic .sty template.
university_style_override: Supervisor/institution requirements override whether first-person is appropriate; never force first person for every thesis or discipline
release_gate: human check authorial voice and factual ownership with manuscript owner; report missing documentary evidence without inventing facts
